events_unavailable_or_incomplete.note: A stock with one of these statuses has no evidence because its filing list could not be read in full; that does not mean no 8-K was filed.

1-2.meaning: missing-delisting-return fill used in the literature, not a measurement of these stocks
1-2.source: Shumway (1997), The Delisting Bias in CRSP Data, Journal of Finance 52(1), 327-340
locators: p. 340 (library PDF page 15): omitted delisting returns average about -30 percent; researchers can test with -0.3 in place of the missing performance delisting return
p. 329 (library PDF page 4), Table I: NYSE/AMEX performance delisting average -41.56 percent where a return exists (11.7 percent of cases)

3.meaning: missing-delisting-return fill used in the literature, not a measurement of these stocks
3.source: Shumway and Warther (1999), The Delisting Bias in CRSP's Nasdaq Data and Its Implications for the Size Effect, Journal of Finance 54(6), 2361-2379
locators: p. 2361 (library PDF page 2), abstract: a corrected return of -55 percent for missing performance-related delisting returns
p. 2370 (library PDF page 11), equation 3: -55 percent after the wider bid-ask gap
p. 2378 (library PDF page 19), conclusion: use -55 percent wherever CRSP shows a missing return for a Nasdaq performance delisting
